STEP 1 - Scene: cooked carrots (sliced halves/chunks), glazed, on a white square plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: square-ish plate, about 24 cm across, so the area is roughly 450 cm² (rounded corners, slightly less than 24x24).

STEP 3 - Items: glazed or cooked carrot pieces, with a light glaze or butter sheen. A few tiny crumbs are negligible.

STEP 4 - Area: the carrots occupy a cluster about 13 cm x 9 cm, which covers roughly 20% of the plate (about 90 cm²). The glaze is included in this.

STEP 5 - Volume: the pieces are about 2 cm thick and are stacked a little in the middle. 90 cm² x 2 cm = 180 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: carrot pieces are fairly dense chunks, so I use a bulk density of 0.65. 180 x 0.65 ≈ 117 g. The pieces are large, with gaps between them, so I take about 115 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: cooked glazed carrots are about 45 kcal/100 g, which gives roughly 52 kcal. I add about 3 g of butter or glaze at 700 kcal/100 g, which gives 21 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: about 118 g for a handful of carrot pieces on a large plate is plausible. Total is about 118 g and 73 kcal.
